title: Sindhu Advances to Hylo Open Quarterfinals
indian_angle: India's top female shuttler PV Sindhu continues her strong run, securing a spot in the Hylo Open quarterfinals.
summary: Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu defeated France’s Pancasari to reach the quarterfinals of the Hylo Open 2026, where she will face Denmark’s Amalie Schulz.

title: Lakshya Sen Defeats Kiran George in All-Indian Hylo Open Clash
indian_angle: A significant all-Indian matchup saw Lakshya Sen triumph over countryman Kiran George, ensuring Indian representation in the Hylo Open quarterfinals.
summary: Lakshya Sen advanced to the Hylo Open quarterfinals after defeating fellow Indian player Kiran George, setting up a clash with the winner of the Aria Dinata-Kalle Koljonen match.

title: Junior World Championships Coaching Camp Begins in Guwahati
indian_angle: This camp at NCE Guwahati is crucial for preparing India's top junior talent for the upcoming BWF World Junior Championships.
summary: A national coaching camp for the BWF World Junior Championships 2026 has commenced at the National Centre of Excellence (NCE) in Guwahati, focusing on preparing India's junior squad.

title: BAI Announces Formation of New Athletes Committee
indian_angle: The formation of the BAI Athletes Committee is a significant step towards ensuring player representation and welfare in Indian badminton governance.
summary: The Badminton Association of India (BAI) has officially announced the formation of its new Athletes Committee, aimed at giving players a stronger voice in decision-making processes.

title: BAI Level-1 Advanced Coaches Course Held in Guwahati & Raipur
indian_angle: This course is vital for upgrading the skills of Indian badminton coaches, contributing to the overall development of the sport nationally.
summary: The BAI successfully conducted its Level-1 (Advanced) Coaches Course at the National Centre of Excellence in Guwahati and Raipur from September 14th to 23rd, 2026.

title: New 3x15 Scoring System Implemented in Domestic Junior Tournaments
indian_angle: This rule change directly impacts Indian junior players and domestic tournaments, potentially altering game dynamics and strategies.
summary: The Badminton Association of India has implemented a new 3x15 scoring system for domestic ranking tournaments and National Championships across U-13, U-15, and U-17 age groups.
